chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who incurred major ritual impurity (janabah) on a cold night, fearing for his life if he were to perform ghusl. He said: 'He should perform tayammum and pray. So when he is safe from the cold, he should perform ghusl and repeat the prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for prayer if one has janabah but fears using water due to cold?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *darar* (harm) in Shia jurisprudence, where the preservation of life overrides the standard requirement of using water for ghusl. It establishes a two-stage process: immediate prayer via tayammum to avoid danger, followed by a mandatory re-performance of the prayer once the specific impediment of cold is removed, highlighting the temporary nature of the concession.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ja’far Bin basher, from the one who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about a man who is hit by the sexual impurity during a cold night, fearing upon himself of the damage if he were to wash’. Heasws said: ‘He should perform Tayammum, and he should pray Salaat. So when he is safe from the cold, he should wash and repeat the Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one who experiences sexual relation during a cold night and is afraid for his life due to Ghusl (bath) because of cold. He (the Imam) said, ‘One must take Tayammum to perform Salah (prayer) and when safe from cold, take Ghusl (bath) and perform such Salah (prayer) again.’”
